stats.why: Twelve years of hit movies, and trans people barely show up.
stats.population: Speaking or named characters in 1,200 top-grossing films, 2014–2025 (100 per year)
stats.report: Inequality in 1,900 Popular Films (August 2026)
stats.caveat: The catch: An independent university count of 1,200 films.

stats.catch: Fewer companies reporting doesn’t mean they dropped their policies.
stats.stat: The number of Fortune 500 companies taking part in HRC's workplace equality index fell 65% in one year, from 377 to 131.
stats.why: When companies go quiet, workers can't tell where they're safe.
stats.population: Fortune 500 companies submitting to HRC's Corporate Equality Index, 2025 vs 2026
stats.report: State of the Workplace for LGBTQ+ Americans and Corporate Equality Index 2026 (Feb 4, 2026)
stats.caveat: The catch: Fewer companies reporting doesn’t mean they dropped their policies.

stats.catch: An online survey of LGBTQ youth, fall 2020.
stats.stat: Of LGBTQ youth who had been kicked out or abandoned by family, 40% said it was because of their LGBTQ identity.
stats.why: Family rejection is a direct road from home to the street.
stats.population: LGBTQ youth ages 13–24 who had slept away from parents or caregivers because they were kicked out or abandoned (14% of 34,759 surveyed)
stats.report: Homelessness and Housing Instability Among LGBTQ Youth (Feb 2022; uses the 2021 National Survey on LGBTQ Youth Mental Health)
stats.caveat: The catch: An online survey of LGBTQ youth, fall 2020.

stats.catch: The question doesn’t say the reason is being LGBT.
stats.stat: 6 in 10 LGBT adults at least sometimes prepare for insults or watch their appearance to be treated fairly at health care visits.
stats.why: Nobody should have to edit themselves to get fair care.
stats.population: U.S. LGBT adults (n=521) vs non-LGBT adults; surveyed June–Aug 2023
stats.report: LGBT Adults’ Experiences with Discrimination and Health Care Disparities: Findings from the KFF Survey of Racism, Discrimination, and Health (Apr 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: The question doesn’t say the reason is being LGBT.

stats.catch: A 2016 experiment with 501 voters in South Florida.
stats.stat: One conversation of about 10 minutes reduced voters' anti-transgender prejudice for at least 3 months.
stats.why: Real conversations about trans lives change minds.
stats.population: 501 voters in South Florida, randomized door-to-door canvassing experiment
stats.report: Durably reducing transphobia: A field experiment on door-to-door canvassing (2016)
stats.caveat: The catch: A 2016 experiment with 501 voters in South Florida.

stats.catch: Students reported their school’s policy themselves.
stats.stat: LGBTQ+ students whose school policy banned all anti-LGBTQ+ bullying attempted suicide in the past year at 10%, versus 22% at schools with no anti-bullying policy.
stats.why: Rules that clearly protect queer students go with less than half the attempt rate.
stats.population: LGBTQ+ young people ages 13–18 enrolled in school in the U.S. (n=10,463)
stats.report: Research brief: Anti-Bullying Policies in School and LGBTQ+ Young People (Oct 2025; 2024 U.S. National Survey data)
stats.caveat: The catch: Students reported their school’s policy themselves.

stats.catch: Data from 2016–2019, before the pandemic.
stats.stat: 8% of transgender adults experienced homelessness in the past year, compared with 1% of cisgender straight adults, a national study found.
stats.why: Trans adults face homelessness at several times the rate of others.
stats.population: U.S. transgender adults (TransPop survey) vs cisgender straight adults; nationally representative samples
stats.org: Williams Institute, UCLA School of Law
stats.report: Homelessness Among LGBT Adults in the US (May 2020)
stats.caveat: The catch: Data from 2016–2019, before the pandemic.

stats.catch: A minimum. Outsports likely missed some.
stats.stat: A record 199 out LGBTQ athletes competed at the Paris 2024 Olympics, up from 186 in Tokyo.
stats.why: Every out Olympian shows a kid they can be both.
stats.population: Publicly out LGBTQ athletes at the Paris 2024 Summer Olympics, Outsports final count
stats.report: Record 199 out LGBTQ athletes made Paris Summer Olympics the gayest ever (Aug 13, 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: A minimum. Outsports likely missed some.

stats.catch: Books with LGBTQ+ characters or people, not themes alone.
stats.stat: In the 2023–24 school year, 1,066 of the 4,218 titles banned in U.S. public schools included LGBTQ+ characters or people.
stats.why: Pulling these books hides queer lives from students.
stats.population: 4,218 unique titles in PEN America's Index of School Book Bans, 2023–24 school year
stats.report: Cover to Cover: An Analysis of Titles Banned in the 23-24 School Year (Feb 2025)
stats.caveat: The catch: Books with LGBTQ+ characters or people, not themes alone.

stats.catch: The exact share wasn’t published, only “more than half.”
stats.stat: In 2024, more than half of LGBTQI+ adults hid a personal relationship to avoid discrimination.
stats.why: Hiding who you love is the daily cost of not feeling safe.
stats.population: U.S. LGBTQI+ adults 18+ (n=1,703), past year; surveyed July 2024
stats.org: Center for American Progress (fielded by NORC at the University of Chicago)
stats.report: The LGBTQI+ Community Reported High Rates of Discrimination in 2024 (CAP LGBTQI+ Community Survey, Wave 3; Mar 12, 2025)
stats.caveat: The catch: The exact share wasn’t published, only “more than half.”

stats.catch: A very large survey, but not a random sample.
stats.stat: 30% of transgender and nonbinary adults in the 2022 U.S. Transgender Survey had experienced homelessness in their lifetime.
stats.why: Almost a third of trans adults have been without a home.
stats.population: Adult respondents (18+) to the 2022 U.S. Transgender Survey (84,170 adults out of 92,329 total)
stats.org: Advocates for Trans Equality (formerly National Center for Transgender Equality)
stats.report: Early Insights: A Report of the 2022 U.S. Transgender Survey (Feb 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: A very large survey, but not a random sample.

stats.catch: Gallup’s count from 2025 phone interviews.
stats.stat: 9% of U.S. adults identify as LGBTQ+, more than double the 3.5% Gallup first measured in 2012.
stats.why: About 1 in 11 adults is LGBTQ+. That's no small group.
stats.population: U.S. adults 18+ (13,454 telephone interviews in 2025)
stats.report: LGBTQ+ Identification Holds at 9% in U.S. (February 16, 2026; 2025 data)
stats.caveat: The catch: Gallup’s count from 2025 phone interviews.

stats.catch: An online survey, not a random sample. Shows a link, not proof of cause.
stats.stat: Trans and nonbinary youth whose caregivers took many or all supportive actions attempted suicide in the past year at 11%, versus 19% with none or very few.
stats.why: Small acts of acceptance at home add up for trans kids.
stats.population: Transgender, nonbinary and gender-questioning young people ages 13–24 in the U.S.
stats.report: Research brief: How to Best Support Transgender and Nonbinary Young People (Nov 2024; 2024 U.S. National Survey data)
stats.caveat: The catch: An online survey, not a random sample. Shows a link, not proof of cause.

stats.catch: A small group, about 80–90 books.
stats.stat: About 64% of picture books banned in U.S. public schools in 2023–24 had LGBTQ+ characters or stories.
stats.why: Young kids lose the chance to see families like theirs, or their classmates'.
stats.population: Banned picture books in PEN America's Index, 2023–24 school year (picture books were 2% of 4,218 banned titles)
stats.report: Cover to Cover: An Analysis of Titles Banned in the 23-24 School Year (Feb 2025)
stats.caveat: The catch: A small group, about 80–90 books.

stats.catch: Not a random sample, and the comparison isn’t age-matched.
stats.stat: Trans and nonbinary adults drank and smoked less than U.S. adults overall, but 35% used marijuana in the past month, vs. 17%.
stats.why: Trans adults' substance use pattern is different, not simply higher.
stats.population: Transgender and nonbinary adults 18+ (2022 USTS, n=84,170) vs U.S. general adult population (2022 NSDUH)
stats.report: Health and Wellbeing: A Report of the 2022 U.S. Transgender Survey (June 2025)
stats.caveat: The catch: Not a random sample, and the comparison isn’t age-matched.

stats.catch: UK football. Reports aren’t incidents, and more people may be reporting.
stats.stat: Reports of homophobia made to football anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out rose 46% to 203 in the 2025/26 season.
stats.why: Hate in the stands keeps queer fans and players away.
stats.population: Discrimination reports received by Kick It Out (UK) from professional, grassroots and online football, 2025/26 season
stats.report: Reporting Statistics: 2025/26 season
stats.caveat: The catch: UK football. Reports aren’t incidents, and more people may be reporting.

stats.catch: From 2021, and a small group.
stats.stat: 58% of transgender and nonbinary adults 45 and older in an AARP survey worry about having to hide their identity to access senior housing.
stats.why: No one should have to go back in the closet to grow old.
stats.population: Transgender and nonbinary adults ages 45+ (n=308) in AARP's online survey of 2,004 LGBTQ adults 45+, fielded Nov 2021
stats.report: Dignity 2022: The Experience of LGBTQ Older Adults (2022)
stats.year: 2021 data; published 2022 (latest edition with this question; Dignity 2024 didn't repeat it)
stats.caveat: The catch: From 2021, and a small group.

stats.catch: Under 30 means ages 18–29.
stats.stat: 23% of U.S. adults under 30 identify as LGBTQ+, compared with 10% of those aged 30 to 49.
stats.why: Nearly 1 in 4 young adults needs to see themselves in leadership.
stats.population: U.S. adults ages 18-29 (Gallup 2025 data)
stats.report: LGBTQ+ Identification Holds at 9% in U.S. (February 16, 2026; 2025 data)
stats.caveat: The catch: Under 30 means ages 18–29.

stats.catch: Arizona only, and a small group.
stats.stat: In Arizona, 22% of trans adults who were unhoused in the past year avoided shelters for fear of mistreatment as trans people.
stats.why: Shelters only help if trans people feel safe walking in.
stats.population: Arizona adult respondents to the 2022 U.S. Transgender Survey who were unhoused in the past year (10% of 1,634 Arizona respondents)
stats.report: 2022 U.S. Transgender Survey – Arizona Report (updated June 2026)
stats.caveat: The catch: Arizona only, and a small group.

stats.catch: An online survey, not a random sample. Shows a link, not proof of cause.
stats.stat: Trans and nonbinary youth with a gender-neutral bathroom at school attempted suicide in the past year at 8%, versus 13% of those without one.
stats.why: A safe bathroom tells trans students they belong at school.
stats.population: Transgender and nonbinary young people ages 13–24 in the U.S.
stats.report: 2025 U.S. National Survey on the Mental Health of LGBTQ+ Young People (newest edition, released 2026)
stats.caveat: The catch: An online survey, not a random sample. Shows a link, not proof of cause.

stats.catch: An opt-in panel. The game count relies on store tags.
stats.stat: 17% of active U.S. PC and console gamers are LGBTQ, but less than 2% of console games have LGBTQ content.
stats.why: Nearly 1 in 5 players are queer, but games barely show them.
stats.population: Active PC/console gamers in the U.S. (Nielsen survey, n=1,452, June–Aug 2023); games tagged LGBTQ in the Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo stores (Nov 2023)
stats.report: The State of LGBTQ Inclusion in Video Games (2024 GLAAD Gaming Report)
stats.caveat: The catch: An opt-in panel. The game count relies on store tags.

stats.catch: A minimum. Outsports later counted 44.
stats.stat: At least 42 out LGBTQ athletes competed at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, a record, up from 12 in Rio 2016.
stats.why: Disabled queer athletes deserve to be seen too.
stats.population: Publicly out LGBTQ athletes at the Paris 2024 Summer Paralympics, per Outsports
stats.report: At least 42 out LGBTQ athletes at Paris Paralympics, a record (Aug 27, 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: A minimum. Outsports later counted 44.

stats.catch: An online panel, not a random sample.
stats.stat: 78% of LGBTQ+ adults 45 and older worry about having enough family or social support as they age.
stats.why: Many LGBTQ+ elders lack family backup; aging services have to plan for that.
stats.population: LGBTQ+ adults ages 45+ (n=2,212); online survey Apr 17–30, 2024
stats.report: Dignity 2024: The Experience of LGBTQ+ Older Adults (Aug 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: An online panel, not a random sample.

stats.catch: Not every state was in the system every year.
stats.stat: Of U.S. suicide deaths in CDC's violent death reporting system from 2013–2019, 84.5% had a missing or unknown sexual orientation.
stats.why: We can't track deaths we don't record.
stats.population: All suicide decedents in CDC's National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS), 2013–2019
stats.report: Limitations of Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity Information as Reported in the National Violent Death Reporting System (LGBT Health 11(3), 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: Not every state was in the system every year.

stats.catch: About 5.3% of all adults.
stats.stat: More than half of LGBTQ+ adults identify as bisexual, about 5% of all U.S. adults.
stats.why: The largest LGBTQ+ group is often the least visible.
stats.population: LGBTQ+ U.S. adults (Gallup 2025 data)
stats.report: LGBTQ+ Identification Holds at 9% in U.S. (February 16, 2026; 2025 data)
stats.caveat: The catch: About 5.3% of all adults.

stats.catch: An advocacy group’s survey, not a random sample.
stats.stat: 62% of LGBTQ+ students said their classes had no LGBTQ+ content; only 27% saw positive LGBTQ+ inclusion.
stats.why: Most queer students never see people like them in what they learn.
stats.population: LGBTQ+ U.S. middle and high school students ages 13+ (grades 6–12, n=2,800), 2023–24 school year
stats.report: The 2025 National School Climate Survey (13th edition, released 2026)
stats.caveat: The catch: An advocacy group’s survey, not a random sample.

stats.catch: From 2022 ads. The only edition so far.
stats.stat: Only 3% of 436 national TV ads from the 10 biggest-spending brands in 2022 were LGBTQ-inclusive.
stats.why: Ads shape what 'normal' looks like, and queer people are barely in them.
stats.population: 436 national linear TV ads (2022) from the top 10 spending brands
stats.report: Advertising Visibility Index 2023 (inaugural edition)
stats.caveat: The catch: From 2022 ads. The only edition so far.

stats.catch: The authors call it a low estimate.
stats.stat: From January 2025 to January 2026, about 360 federal data collections removed at least one sexual orientation or gender identity measure.
stats.why: Includes the national systems that track suicidal thoughts and suicide deaths.
stats.population: U.S. federal data collections, including NSDUH (sexual orientation and gender identity) and CDC's NVDRS (gender identity)
stats.org: Williams Institute, UCLA School of Law (Bouton, Redfield)
stats.report: Removal of Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity from Federal Data Collections: January 2025 to January 2026 (Feb 2026)
stats.caveat: The catch: The authors call it a low estimate.

stats.catch: Only 23% of programs answered.
stats.stat: U.S. residency programs surveyed in 2023–24 spent a median of just 2 classroom hours a year on LGBTQ health; 15.8% spent none.
stats.why: Doctors can't care well for people their training barely mentions.
stats.population: 1,048 U.S. graduate medical education (residency) programs that responded (23.2% of 4,512) in the 2023–2024 ERAS cycle; surveyed Sept 2023–Aug 2024
stats.report: Evaluating the inclusion of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer-related content in graduate medical education: a national survey of program directors (BMC Med Educ, Jul 2025)
stats.caveat: The catch: Only 23% of programs answered.

stats.catch: 148 riders, mostly in Europe, who chose to answer.
stats.stat: 54% of LGBTQ+ cyclists surveyed named lack of representation as a main barrier to LGB inclusion in cycling.
stats.why: Queer riders can't be what they can't see.
stats.population: 148 sexual and/or gender minority cyclists (mostly in Europe) in an online survey, Aug–Oct 2022
stats.org: International Review for the Sociology of Sport (peer-reviewed; Hardwicke, Roberts, Anderson & Magrath)
stats.report: Drafting behind LGB: Transgender athletes in the sport of cycling (2023; vol. 59, issue 1)
stats.caveat: The catch: 148 riders, mostly in Europe, who chose to answer.

stats.catch: An estimate built from national health surveys.
stats.stat: Over 2.8 million people ages 13 and older in the U.S. identify as transgender, about 1% of that age group.
stats.why: Millions of trans Americans are affected by laws written about them.
stats.population: U.S. adults 18+ and youth 13-17
stats.org: Williams Institute, UCLA School of Law
stats.report: How Many Adults and Youth Identify as Transgender in the United States? (August 2025)
stats.caveat: The catch: An estimate built from national health surveys.

stats.catch: Compared with low-to-moderate family support.
stats.stat: Only 17% of trans and nonbinary youth of color had high family support; those who did had 34% lower odds of attempting suicide in the past year.
stats.why: Family acceptance protects, but too few trans youth of color get it.
stats.population: Transgender, nonbinary and gender-questioning young people of color ages 13–24 in the U.S. (n=4,122)
stats.report: Research brief: Friends, Family, and Community: Social Support and the Health of Transgender and Nonbinary Young People of Color (Aug 2025; 2024 U.S. National Survey data)
stats.caveat: The catch: Compared with low-to-moderate family support.

stats.catch: Only people who chose transgender alone. HUD’s 2025 report dropped it.
stats.stat: On one night in January 2024, HUD counted 2,561 people experiencing homelessness who identified solely as transgender (people who also selected another gender were counted separately).
stats.why: You can't help people a count refuses to see.
stats.population: People experiencing sheltered or unsheltered homelessness on a single night, U.S. Point-in-Time count, January 2024
stats.org: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
stats.report: The 2024 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report (AHAR) to Congress, Part 1: Point-in-Time Estimates (Dec 2024)
stats.caveat: The catch: Only people who chose transgender alone. HUD’s 2025 report dropped it.
